Question: Why do I feel worthless after finding out my cousin's boyfriend is a successful entrepreneur with old money?
Answer: Thanks for the A2A.It sounds to me like the issue isn't really with your relationship with your cousin, but with your own idea of success. Consider this: When it comes right down to it, the way you feel is entirely up to you. You want good, positive feelings in your life, right? Then force yourself to focus on the positive aspects of your relationship and just let the negative things fade into the background. I'm a professional musician, and every time I perform I have to manage personal relationships with everyone else on stage. For example, today I had to play a very modern piece of music that until today has made me very uncomfortable. There really isn't any kind of melody. Just an orchestra making lots of random noises with their instruments. When we rehearsed the piece yesterday, I left feeling angry and vaguely nauseated. I wanted to find the composer and make her feel as awful as her music made me feel. Then this morning before rehearsal, it occurred to me that her music didn't "make" me do anything. I was the one focusing on the elements of the piece that made me uncomfortable and allowing my attitude to ruin the entire experience. So today I refused to give any energy to the negative thoughts and focus entirely on making beauty no matter what. It was wonderful. I left rehearsal today with a smile on my face. Give it a try when you're around your cousin. Really notice and appreciate the positive side of things. You can't control how or what other people's attitudes are, but you can certainly control your own.

Question: How does a band minimize the undesired resonance from a drumset during a live musical performance or during a practice session?
Answer: They put the drummer inside a plexiglass enclosure. I've played many Broadway musical tours, and that's how the sound guys do it in the pit. It works really well. You can have a flute player just a few feet away and still hear them just fine through the mic.

Question: Are there some siblings who, due to some quirk of biology, don't feel sexual repulsion but rather sexual attraction to each other?
Answer: Attraction between siblings is not a quirk of biology, it's a psychological problem. It's biologically completely normal for two sexually mature people to be attracted to each other. It is having a healthy psychosocial relationship that prevents incest. When incest happens, there is something seriously wrong in the psychological development of one or both parties involved.
